goal: Upgrade tilemap rendering from solid-color rects to atlas-based sprite rendering. Adds an `AtlasTilemap` class that reads a Tiled-style JSON map plus a sprite atlas and emits drawSprite calls to the existing Renderer. The Phase-1 placeholder Tilemap stays for tests; this is the production renderer path.
constraints: Class `AtlasTilemap` constructor: `{ map: TilemapData, atlas: Atlas, layer?: RenderLayer }`. Default layer = 'world'.

Map shape (subset of Tiled JSON): `TilemapData = { width: number; height: number; tileSize: number; layers: TileLayer[] }`. `TileLayer = { name: string; data: number[]; visible?: boolean }`. Each `data[i]` is a tile index into the atlas frames; 0 = empty (no draw).
Atlas frame lookup: tile index N maps to the atlas frame named `tile-${N}` (a convention; documented in JSDoc). Tile index 0 is reserved for empty.
API: `render(renderer: Renderer, camera?: Camera): void` queues drawSprite calls for every non-empty visible tile within the camera viewport (or all tiles if no camera).
Frustum culling: if a camera is provided, only emit tiles whose pixel rect intersects the camera's view rect. (Camera has a `position` and the renderer has RENDER_W/RENDER_H constants.)
All draw positions snapped to integer pixels via `Math.round`.

Test stub: pass a fake atlas (Map<string, Sprite>) and a fake Renderer with a recording drawSprite. Assert the queued draws match the expected (layer, frame, x, y) tuples for both with-camera and no-camera paths.
acceptance: Test: a 3x3 map with tiles [0,1,0; 1,2,1; 0,1,0] queues exactly 5 drawSprite calls when no camera is given.
Test: same map with a camera positioned so only the top-left quadrant is in view queues 2 drawSprite calls (frustum cull).
Test: an invisible layer is skipped entirely.
Test: tile index 0 is never drawn.
Test: empty atlas frame for an index throws a clear error at render time.
